hints: Focus on what each test is really asking you, one is for the carbonyl group and the other two are for easily oxidised groups.
An orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH tells you T must contain a C=O group, so it is an aldehyde or a ketone.
No reaction with both Fehling's and acidified dichromate rules out aldehydes and alcohols, leaving only a simple ketone with no OH group.
walkthrough:
**Read the 2,4-DNPH result**

Great start here. 2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} + \text{2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Use Fehling's to split aldehyde from ketone**

Fehling's solution is a mild oxidising agent. It oxidises aldehydes but not ketones.

Test rule:
$$\text{RCHO} + \text{Fehling's (blue)} \rightarrow \text{brick-red precipitate}$$ $$\text{RCOR'} + \text{Fehling's} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$
Since T shows no reaction, T cannot be an aldehyde. It must be a ketone.

**Confirm with acidified dichromate**

Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes and acids, secondary alcohols to ketones, and aldehydes to acids.

Test rule:
$$\text{orange } \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \rightarrow \text{green } \text{Cr}^{3+} \text{ if oxidation occurs}$$
No reaction means T has no primary alcohol, no secondary alcohol and no aldehyde. This fits perfectly with a simple ketone.

**Match to the structures**

Option D, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOCH}_3$, is 3-methylbutan-2-one, a ketone with no OH group. It gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test and is resistant to both Fehling's and acidified dichromate.

options.A: Option A is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$, an aldehyde. It would give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH, but it would also reduce Fehling's to a brick-red precipitate and turn acidified dichromate from orange to green. Both contradict the no reaction results.
options.B: Option B is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol. It has no C=O group so it would give no precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It would also be oxidised by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, so it fails two of the observations.
options.C: Option C is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COCH}_3$, a hydroxy-ketone. The ketone part gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test, but the secondary $\text{OH}$ group is oxidised by acidified dichromate (orange to green). Alpha-hydroxy ketones also reduce Fehling's, so it would not show two no reactions.
options.D: Option D is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOCH}_3$, a ketone with no alcohol group. The C=O gives the orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH, while ketones resist oxidation by Fehling's and by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, giving no reaction in both. This matches all three results.
